theARKANSASBLANKFIELDSQUESTION.whyTheCLIPPINGPassIsCorrect: The obligation asks whether anything on the delivered page is clipped, truncated, or drawn over the form. On these bytes nothing is: 0 of 34 text-carrying appearances exceed their own clip window, 0 px of added ink falls outside a declared write rectangle, and 0 px of the form's printed ink has been removed on any of 32 pages. Refusal is a legitimate way to reach that zero, and the specific danger of reaching a clipping zero dishonestly - shrinking a value until it fits and calling that a repair, or truncating the string while leaving the text layer whole so a text-only check still reads it - is exactly what did NOT happen: no appearance was resized, reflowed or moved, the text layer no longer carries the value either, and the build records notTruncated true against each refusal with the usable width it was measured against. The build composes a participant-facing sentence for each refusal and files it in reports/rendered-artifacts.json and reports/actual-writes.json, which are internal review artifacts. On the delivered documents the phrases 'does not fit', 'by hand', 'too long', 'truncat' and 'smallest readable' occur 0 times, and 'Case No' occurs 0 times in participant-instructions.md. An undisclosed OMISSION is strictly larger than the undisclosed reformat that failed Maine's KNOWN_PREFILLS on this same return.
